name: Waldeyer’s neuron-doctrine synthesis
description: Waldeyer synthesized a view of nerve cells as distinct units of nervous tissue and named the unit neuron.

impact.note: Gave neuroscientists the neuron as the distinct unit of the nervous system, a new understanding on which later neuroanatomy and physiology were built.

date.basis: Year is the date of the described episode in the cited source, not necessarily the invention or first conception.

events.statement: Waldeyer published a review synthesizing evidence for the neuron doctrine and introducing neuron terminology.

evidence.supports: Dates Waldeyer’s neuron-doctrine synthesis to 1891 and identifies prior contributions by Forel and others.

contributions.resource: Synthesized earlier evidence and published the review.

evidence.supports: Dates Waldeyer’s neuron-doctrine synthesis to 1891 and identifies prior contributions by Forel and others.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest episode established from the sources collected for this scoped record, not a claim of global priority.

caveats: Earlier contributors included Forel, His and Ramón y Cajal; the 1891 review was a synthesis, not an independent discovery of nerve cells. Historians dispute the allocation of credit.

research.note: Independent second reading checked the dated event evidence; other facets remain as previously assessed.
